_comment: EXAMPLE TWIN - obviously-fake contents. This documents the SHAPE of the fleet's
Claude account pool. The real file lives OUTSIDE this skill tree, in the
organization secrets, at the path config's accounts.pool_file names, mode 0600.
This twin is here so a fresh clone is legible; NEVER put a real credential in
this tree.
A JSON LIST, one object per account: username, password, token_file, home_agent.
An entry carries a password (what a login agent's browser sign-in types), a
token_file (the account's long-lived token from claude setup-token, which a token
agent runs with: an environment file, mode 0600, with a '# fleet-auth: token' and a
'# fleet-account: <username>' header), or both. Accounts enter the pool only through
`pool_pick.py --register` (SKILL.md step 5), never by editing this file. The pool
covers the CLAUDE LOGIN ONLY, which governs the token quota and nothing else,
so its accounts belong to no agent: any agent may be signed in with any of
them. home_agent records which agent the account was issued for and plays no
part in choosing one. Which agent holds which account right now is the LEASE
file (accounts.lease_file), never this one, and which account an agent goes
to next is `pool_pick.py`'s answer (SKILL.md step 5) - list order means
nothing.
During a revival the PASSWORD of the ONE chosen entry is read from this file
inside the sign-in driver's own process and typed straight into the browser
(SKILL.md step 6). Nothing that records - a command line, a shell history, a
tool result, a transcript - ever holds it. On the step-7 fallback that one
entry is handed to a HUMAN (named in CONTEXT.md) so they can sign the agent in
in a real browser; never the whole file, only to that person, only over the
channel the charter names, and never logged.
The pool picker and tmux_triage.sh --accounts print usernames and never a
password, so nobody has to cat this file. Its tests run fixtures, never it.
